subject: English Language
examFormat: The syllabus (Use of English) aims to guide candidates in preparing for the UTME and evaluates their ability to communicate effectively in written and spoken English and to use English for learning at the tertiary level. It has three sections: Comprehension and Summary, Lexis and Structure, and Oral Forms. The paper has 60 questions in total: Section A 21 (1 comprehension passage 5, 1 summary passage 5, 1 cloze passage 10, 1 reading text 5), Section B 25 (sentence interpretation 5, antonyms 5, synonyms 5, basic grammar 10), Section C 10 (vowels, consonants, rhymes, word stress, emphatic stress, 2 each).
excluded: The syllabus does not name the Approved Reading Text (novel); it only says one reading text carries 5 questions, so no prescribed text could be listed.

topics.name: Comprehension and Summary
objectives: identify main points/topic sentences in passages
identify the grammatical functions of words, phrases, clauses and figurative/idiomatic expressions
deduce or infer the writers' intentions including mood, attitude to the subject matter and opinion
topics.content: Three passages are to be set (one of them a cloze test), reflecting various disciplines and about 200 words long each. Passages may be descriptive, narrative, expository or argumentative/persuasive. Questions test comprehension of the whole or part of each passage; comprehension of words, phrases, clauses, sentences, figures of speech and idioms as used in the passages; coherence and logical reasoning (deductions, inferences, etc.); the Approved Reading Text; and synthesis of ideas from the passages. Synthesis of ideas means the art of combining distinct or separate pieces of information to form a complete whole as summary.

subtopics.name: Comprehension of whole or part of passage
Comprehension of words, phrases, clauses, sentences, figures of speech and idioms

topics.name: Lexis and Structure
objectives: identify words and expressions in their ordinary, figurative and idiomatic contexts
determine similar and opposite meanings of words
differentiate between correct and incorrect spellings
identify various grammatical patterns in use
topics.content: Idioms to be tested are those that are formal and expressed in Standard British English (SBE). Mood, tense, aspect, number, agreement/concord, degree (positive, comparative and superlative) and question tags are covered under grammar.

subtopics.name: Mood, tense, aspect, number, agreement/concord, degree and question tags

topics.name: Oral Forms
objectives: identify correct pronunciation of individual words and articulation of connected speech
topics.content: Emphatic stress involves the placement of stress on words in an utterance for the purpose of emphasis.
